observationsNotFindings: STRUCTURAL THINNESS, recorded for the third consecutive subject and again not charged on its own. At 7493 bytes this file sits with G26 v1 (4549) and G27 v1 (5315) well below the fuller harness specifications I accepted earlier this session (G19 33369, G22 39418, G23 38890), and the same eighteen top-level keys common to all three fuller siblings are absent, including whatThisCloses, failsIf, a corpus block, a platforms block and a top-level passProperty. All five members also omit the measures field. Unlike G26 and G27, this file's thinness did produce a chargeable consequence - the missing citation at EV-3 - which is why the finding above is stated as a specific unfulfilled action rather than as thinness.

The file supplies no mapping from the seven EE classes to the five members, and no per-EE exactByteIntent, where G22 mapped NT-TCB-1..4 to witnessing members and G23 gave each NT class its own exactByteIntent and passProperty. namedExecutesLimbs lists the seven ids and nothing binds them to EV-1..EV-5 except EV-2's parenthetical '(EE-5b)'. Not charged - the ids are verified correct and the live evidence cell, not the EE list, defines the members - but a reader cannot tell from this file which member scores EE-1 versus EE-4.

EV-1 enumerates six of the live claim's seven excluded forms. I checked and this is correct rather than a drop: the seventh, represented pre-stage imperative substitution, is EV-2's subject, following the live evidence cell's own admission-time / post-admission division and D-157's record of section 7 item 8's two disjunctive fates.

No OBL id is named and there is no whatThisCloses block, so the refusal of closure-by-existence rests on one authorityClaim sentence, which does carry it. The dispatch again writes 'the corresponding OBL-*-HARNESS-SPEC' with a wildcard.
